chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Similar to it, and there is an increase in it: 'If a man were to apply kohl in his eye from wine with an applicator, it would be deserving upon Allah that He apply fire in his eye with an applicator.'

key_terms.نَارٍ: Fire (often referring to Hellfire or divine punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of using wine as kohl according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the principle of proportional retribution (muqabalah) in divine justice, where the specific use of wine as a cosmetic leads to a corresponding application of fire in the Hereafter. It underscores the severity of intoxicants by extending their penalty beyond consumption to their physical application, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible consequences of sin. The metaphor serves as a vivid reminder that the instrument of sin becomes the instrument of punishment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from his father, from Abu Abdullahasws

, similar to it, and there is an increase in it, ‘(Heasws having said: ‘If a man were to apply kohl in his eyes from wine with an applicator, would be deserving to Allahazwj that Heazwj Apply Fire (in his eyes) with an applicator’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Ali, from his father from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.

He has added, ‘If a man uses wine of an amount equal to the amount of the kohl (eyeliner) powder picked up by an kohl (eyeliner) powder applicator, it becomes a right on Allah to apply the same amount of kohl (eyeliner) of the fire on him.’”
